text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AD-DUSTOUR

- Why has King Hussein rung the alarm bells? Information Minister talks about the background to the crisis with Israel. Says suspicions increased after Israeli practices in wake of the recent visit of Prime Minister Netanyahu's adviser to Jordan
- Bread price could drop soon in light of the anticipated decision to purchase 150,000 tonnes of wheat in this week's tender.
- Jordan's ambassador to Israel says timing of Israeli President's visit to Jordan to be decided in two days.
- Arrival of a batch of Palestinians injured during "al-Aqsa mosque (Moslem site in Jerusalem) intifada (uprising)" for treatment in Jordanian hospitals.
- Palestinian President Arafat to visit Jordan in the next few days. A possible tripartite summit in Aqaba between King Hussein, Egyptian President Mubarak and Palestinian leader Arafat.
AL-RAI
- Prime Minister Kabariti meets Sheikh Nahnah of the Algerian Hamas movement: both stress the depth of Jordanian-Algerian ties.
- Doctors insist on their pay rise demands, will meet the health minister next Tuesday.
- French President Chirac visits Jordan on October 23, will address parliament.
- Jordan says Israel "lacks the real desire to implement peace accords and the danger of Netanyahu's position lies in the reopening of the accords files."
- Parliament Speaker says the policies of Netanyahu are a declaration of war on the peace process.
- Political parties call for "a united position to face Israeli intransigence."
JORDAN TIMES
- Bread prices could be reduced in view of drop in world wheat prices.
- News Analysis: Netanyahu does not seem to have received Jordan's message yet.
- Jordanian embassy in Tel Aviv receives threats.
AL ASWAQ
- Kabariti says Arafat to brief King Hussein on course of negotiations.
- Minister of Adminstrative Development Nasser says priority in civil service employment given to unemployed.
- Partial solar eclipse seen from Western Europe to Canada.
